evaluated.name: GrossProfitVsWorkingCapitalPressure
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profitability is a clean top-line measure of business quality, but it is only credible when it is not being manufactured by expanding working capital; industry-adjusted gross profit combined with low working-capital accrual pressure identifies genuinely efficient franchises.
evaluated.reasoning: Using gross profit avoids contamination from the same accrual items that appear in the accrual leg, making the two channels economically independent inputs rather than mechanical mirror images. Industry ranking of gross profitability handles the large cross-industry dispersion in cost structure, while the balance-sheet accrual leg captures receivable/inventory-financed sales growth.

evaluated.name: MarginGainFinancedByWorkingCapital
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross-margin expansion that is simultaneously financed by a build-up in receivables and inventory reflects channel stuffing, loosened credit terms, or unsold production rather than real pricing power, so such profitability gains predict negative future abnormal returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This uses income-statement margin dynamics against specific cash-flow-statement working-capital components rather than the total earnings-minus-cash wedge, so it is not the sign-flipped complement of any level-based profitability-times-accrual product. The COALESCE fallback to the balance-sheet change in non-cash current assets is economically equivalent in sign and preserves coverage for firms and periods where the cash-flow-statement detail lines are unreported.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TaxValidatedProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Pretax profits are credible when the firm actually settles the associated tax liability in cash; when reported pretax income rises while income taxes payable balloon, the book-tax gap signals aggressive or non-cash income recognition that reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: The tax-accrual channel is a validation test that is independent of the working-capital accrual anomaly and of RMW-style profitability, because taxes payable respond to the credibility of income recognition rather than to operating asset growth. Interacting it with pretax profitability is essential: a shrinking tax payable is uninformative for loss-makers, so the joint state carries the economic content.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitPremiumWeightedByAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality is not a separate return driver but a credibility weight on profitability: the profitability premium should be strongly positive among clean-accrual firms and attenuate toward zero among accrual-financed firms, whose reported profitability conveys no information.
evaluated.reasoning: The centered profitability z-score multiplied by a bounded [0,1] quality weight implements regime-dependent pricing continuously — accrual-heavy firms collapse toward zero regardless of profitability, with no point mass and no masking artifact — which is exactly the conditional structure the earlier indicator gate failed to deliver. Paired with signal 4 on identical legs, it tells us whether the interaction is best expressed as a conjunction or as an attenuation of the profitability slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitsFlatteredBySupplierCredit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Liability-side accruals behave oppositely to asset-side accruals: profitable firms whose cash generation is being supported by stretching accounts payable and other operating liabilities are borrowing liquidity from suppliers, and this financing source reverses, so their apparent profitability is fragile.
evaluated.reasoning: Standard accrual measures net operating liabilities against operating assets, which assumes the two sides carry identical information; decomposing them and interacting only the liability side with profitability is a directionally novel test rather than a re-scaling of Sloan accruals. The COALESCE fallback from the cash-flow-statement payables line to the change in non-debt current liabilities is sign-consistent and preserves coverage in pre-1988 and sparsely reported firm-years.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitsThatCompoundIntoCash
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(SUB(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Over a multi-year horizon, genuine profitability shows up as a rising cash stock, whereas accrual-supported profitability shows up as a permanently expanding non-cash current-asset base; the five-year divergence between these two accumulation paths separates earnings that were actually collected from earnings that were only booked.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the one-year flow comparison (which the critic correctly identified as an affine restatement of the archived Sloan-style accrual leg) with a stock-accumulation trajectory: a firm can have clean accruals in any single year yet still never convert a decade of reported profit into cash, and only the trend contrast detects that. Because the accrual leg is a five-year slope of balance-sheet stocks rather than a scaled annual accrual, it is not spanned by CMA-style asset-growth or by cash-based profitability, and the three-year averaged profitability leg ensures the interaction conditions on a persistent profit state.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ChronicAccrualRelianceOnProfits
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 0), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The frequency, not the size, of accrual reliance is what distinguishes benign working-capital timing from systematic earnings support: a profitable firm that posts income-increasing accruals in nearly every one of the last five years is running a chronic recognition policy whose reversal is inevitable, whereas a firm with one large accrual year is usually just lumpy.
evaluated.reasoning: Counting positive-accrual years converts the accrual leg into a persistence statistic that is unit-free and immune to the negative-denominator and outlier problems that sank the GROWTH-based construction, so the ranking is stable across retailers, subscription firms, and asset-light businesses. The count is nearly uncorrelated with the magnitude-based accrual factor exposure embedded in the archive, so the profitability interaction is being tested against a genuinely different accrual construct rather than a rescaling of it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitabilityWithStableAccrualProcess
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality in the Dechow-Dichev sense is a second-moment property: profitable firms whose working-capital accrual process is erratic have low-precision earnings maps to cash and their reported profitability is a noisy signal of future profitability, so the market over-relies on it.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the conjunction-versus-product functional-form question entirely and changes the economic content of the accrual leg from level to instability, which is a distinct construct: a firm with persistently large but predictable accruals scores well here and badly on the archived level-based signal. Volatility of accruals is a measurement-precision concept rather than a growth or investment concept, so it is far less likely to be absorbed by RMW and CMA loadings that flattened the earlier FF5 alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitXReceivableInventoryRelease
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(ADD(recch, invch), NEG(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1))), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The asset side of the operating cycle carries the earnings-quality information: profitable firms that collect receivables and turn inventory into cash have realized sales, whereas equally profitable firms whose margins are accompanied by receivable and inventory build are recognizing revenue that has not been collected.
evaluated.reasoning: Paired with signal 1, this isolates exactly which half of the operating cycle produced the archive's strongest alpha — an identical profitability leg and scaling, with only the accrual component swapped, so the comparison is clean. Note that generation 0 tested this component against a *margin-change* profitability leg and found nothing, so this also tells us whether the profitability leg must be a level rather than a change for the interaction to fire.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PersistentCashCycleReleaseWithProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(ADD(apalch, ADD(recch, invch)), NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of working-capital release can be liquidation or a demand shock, but five years of cumulative release alongside sustained operating profitability identifies a structurally cash-generative operating model whose reported profits require no incremental working-capital investment to sustain.
evaluated.reasoning: Cumulating the working-capital cash flow over five years averages out the mean-reverting timing noise that makes one-year accrual measures fragile, while smoothing profitability over three years ensures the interaction conditions on a persistent profit state rather than a single strong year. If the five-year version dominates the one-year version in FF5 alpha, the mechanism is a durable business-model attribute; if it is weaker, the archive's result is a short-horizon cash-timing effect and future refinements should stay at annual frequency.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SupplyChainPowerVsPaymentStretch
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(MIN(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(invch, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Extending payables is a sign of bargaining power only when inventory is simultaneously being converted to cash; a profitable firm that stretches suppliers while inventory piles up is delaying payment because goods are not selling, and that state reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than re-running the generation-0 aggregate working-capital test that already produced a null alpha, this conditions the proven payables leg on the inventory leg through a weakest-link MIN, which separates genuine supply-chain power from distress-driven payment stretching — two states the additive aggregate deliberately merges. It therefore refines the archive's strongest result instead of diluting it with untested components.

evaluated.name: MarginPowerXSupplierCredit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The supplier-credit interaction should operate through pricing power rather than capital efficiency: firms with high gross margins have differentiated products and therefore also command favorable trade terms, so the joint state of high margin and expanding supplier financing identifies real market power rather than asset-light accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the profitability leg along the DuPont margin-versus-turnover decomposition while leaving the accrual leg exactly as in the archive's winner, so the comparison identifies which component of profitability the trade-credit mechanism actually interacts with — an economic question, not a denominator rescaling of the accrual leg. Sales-scaled margin is also stable and well defined for essentially all operating firms, avoiding the low-COGS instability that the cogs-scaled version would have introduced.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeDepreciationCashProfits
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms with equally strong pre-depreciation operating profitability, those recording heavy depreciation accruals report depressed bottom-line earnings; investors anchor on reported earnings and underprice these firms even though their cash-generating capacity, which the depreciation accrual does not touch, is identical.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the operating-liability family entirely and tests the one large non-cash accrual whose economics run opposite to working-capital accruals: depreciation lowers earnings without lowering cash, so conservatism creates an earnings-versus-cash wedge in the direction of underpricing rather than overpricing. Using EBITDA-level profitability is essential because depreciation does not enter oibdp, making the interaction a clean test of accounting conservatism rather than a mechanical decomposition of the same quantity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SupplierCreditRegimeByProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Expanding supplier credit means opposite things in opposite profitability regimes: for profitable firms it is negotiated financing that funds a self-sustaining operating cycle, while for unprofitable firms it is forced liquidity management that precedes distress, so the return effect of the payables flow should flip sign across the profitability distribution.
evaluated.reasoning: Centering the profitability leg makes the short leg consist of unprofitable firms that are expanding supplier credit rather than merely profitable firms with weak payables flow, which is the direct test of whether the archive's best result is a genuine interaction or a standalone payables effect riding on a profitability tilt. The tax-and-other-operating discrimination test it replaces was compromised by the undefined aoloch catch-all and by duplicating an already-flat tax leg, so this substitutes a sharper and better-measured discrimination.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IndustryNeutralSupplierCreditProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Trade-credit norms are industry-determined — retailers and wholesalers structurally run large payables while software and services run almost none — so the informative quantity is a profitable firm's payables expansion relative to its own industry's payment conventions, not relative to the whole market.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's winner ranks the payables flow cross-sectionally, which means its long leg is likely concentrated in a handful of trade-credit-intensive industries; industry-ranking the accrual leg removes that composition tilt and tests whether the alpha survives as a within-industry bargaining-power effect. If alpha holds or strengthens with more stable portfolio composition, the mechanism is firm-level supplier power; if it collapses, the archive result was an industry bet and future work should look elsewhere.

evaluated.name: SustainedSupplierFinancingWithProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of payables expansion can be a timing artifact around fiscal year-end, but three consecutive years of cumulative supplier financing alongside high gross profitability reflects negotiated terms that suppliers have conceded permanently to a strong counterparty.
evaluated.reasoning: The five-year cumulative version bundled all three working-capital components and produced only 1.0% alpha, so this isolates the proven payables component at a shorter, coverage-preserving horizon to see whether persistence adds to or dilutes the one-year effect. Cumulating also averages out year-end payment-timing noise without imposing the five-year cash-flow-item history that cut coverage in earlier temporal signals.

evaluated.name: FreeSupplierCreditNotCostlyDebt
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The supplier-credit premium should reflect access to *free*, non-interest-bearing financing; a profitable firm that expands payables while simultaneously drawing down short-term debt is substituting cheap for expensive capital, whereas one expanding both is simply levering up its liquidity and is not exhibiting bargaining power.
evaluated.reasoning: Netting the change in current debt against the payables flow separates negotiated trade terms from general liability expansion, which is the leading benign explanation for the archive's strongest result and one no prior signal has controlled for. It also mechanically excludes distressed firms that stretch suppliers while rolling short-term borrowings, which should clean up the short leg and improve alpha precision.

evaluated.name: TwoChannelAccrualCredibilityProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Supplier-financed cash generation and conservative non-cash charges are independent forms of accrual credibility — one shows profits are self-funding, the other shows profits are understated — so profitable firms exhibiting both should be the most systematically underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: The two accrual channels with the best evidence so far use different data sources and have low economic overlap (trade terms versus fixed-asset accounting), so averaging their ranks should raise the signal-to-noise of the quality leg without narrowing coverage the way a MIN conjunction did. This is the batch's consolidation test: if the combined version beats both parents on alpha and Sharpe, later generations should build on the composite rather than on either channel alone.

evaluated.name: AcceleratingDepreciationConservatism
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Capital intensity is a slow-moving structural attribute, so a year-over-year rise in the depreciation charge per dollar of assets reflects an accounting policy shift toward shorter useful lives or faster write-offs; for firms with strong pre-depreciation profitability this conservatism depresses reported earnings without touching cash generation, and earnings-anchored investors underprice them.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the depreciation *level* with its first difference removes the capital-intensity confound that industry-ranking could not fix, because within a firm the asset base changes slowly while the charge rate reflects management's estimate choices. The interaction remains essential: rising depreciation is only an understatement-of-profit story for firms whose EBITDA-level profitability is genuinely high, and oibdp excludes depreciation so the two legs are not mechanically linked.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TradeTermsBeyondPurchaseGrowth
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(cogs, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Payables expand mechanically when a firm simply buys more inputs, so genuine bargaining power is payables growth in excess of purchase growth: profitable firms lengthening payment terms faster than their cost base is expanding are extracting real financing concessions from suppliers, and that advantage is durable and underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the tax-timing re-run, whose sign contradiction and sparse population would have made the result uninterpretable, and substitutes the discrimination test that actually matters for the archive's strongest signal — whether the payables premium is trade-term extension or merely a volume artifact of input growth. Both legs use well-populated income-statement and cash-flow items with a common asset scaling, so the difference is dimensionally coherent and coverage stays at the level of the existing winner.

evaluated.name: IndustryNeutralFreeSupplierCredit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitable firms that expand non-interest-bearing supplier financing while not increasing short-term borrowing are obtaining free capital on the strength of their franchise, and this advantage is best measured against the trade-credit conventions of their own industry rather than against the market as a whole.
evaluated.reasoning: The two independently validated improvements to the archive's core signal — netting short-term debt (alpha 4.6%, t 5.41) and industry-ranking the accrual leg (Sharpe 0.302) — address different confounds (distress-driven liability expansion versus industry composition), so combining them should compound rather than offset. This is the batch's primary consolidation candidate.

evaluated.name: NegativeCashCycleProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The flow results point to a structural attribute: profitable firms that operate a negative cash conversion cycle — customers and suppliers fund the operating cycle so that net operating working capital per dollar of sales is minimal or negative — run self-financing business models whose profits require no incremental capital and are therefore more durable than the market prices.
evaluated.reasoning: Scaling net operating working capital by sales converts the stock into a cash-conversion-cycle measure in units of revenue-days, which is an operating-efficiency construct rather than the asset-scaled operating-liability leverage that was previously flagged as a Penman–Nissim rediscovery. It also tests whether the archive's flow-based finding reflects a permanent business-model characteristic or only annual payment timing, using widely populated balance-sheet items.

evaluated.name: NetSupplyChainCreditPosition
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(apalch, recch), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the firm's net position as a supply-chain financier: profitable firms that simultaneously take more credit from suppliers and extend less to customers are net borrowers within the value chain, which reflects bargaining power on both sides and frees capital, whereas firms doing the reverse are subsidizing their trading partners.
evaluated.reasoning: The payables and receivables flows have both shown strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but only payables produced FF5 alpha, so netting them into a single directional trade-credit position tests whether the receivables side adds incremental power once expressed in the same economic direction rather than as a separate quality screen. Inventory is deliberately excluded because it is a production decision, not a credit decision, and its inclusion diluted the five-year cumulative version.

evaluated.name: OperatingProfitXSupplierCredit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If supplier credit certifies overall firm quality, the interaction should be at least as strong with operating profitability after overheads as with gross profitability; if it is specifically gross profitability that matters, the mechanism is about the goods trade relationship rather than about general financial strength.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong archive result uses the gross-profit leg, so the marginal value of the profitability definition has never been measured against the winning accrual leg — a cheap, high-information discrimination test with identical scaling and combination structure. evaluated.name: SupplierCreditSurpriseVsOwnHistory
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: If trade-credit expansion is informed certification, what carries information is a *change in suppliers' assessment* of the firm, which means payables growth that is unusual relative to the firm's own five-year history rather than merely high relative to other firms.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal normalizes the payables flow cross-sectionally, so firms with permanently credit-intensive operating models sit in the long leg year after year; time-series ranking within the firm strips out that fixed component and tests whether the premium comes from the news content of newly extended terms. This is a different normalization axis from the industry-neutral test rather than another cross-sectional rescaling, and it directly discriminates a stable business-model interpretation from a certification-news interpretation.

evaluated.name: PredictableProfitsWithSupplierCredit
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Suppliers extend terms on the basis of predictability as much as level: a firm whose gross profitability is both high and stable presents low counterparty risk, so trade-credit expansion granted to such a firm is a far stronger certification of durable earnings than the same expansion granted to a firm with erratic profits.
evaluated.reasoning: Profit-level volatility is a second moment that is not collinear with the level, so unlike a three-year moving average it adds genuinely new cross-sectional information to the profitability leg rather than reproducing it with autocorrelation near 0.9. The test is economically decisive for the certification story: if adding predictability strengthens alpha, suppliers are pricing earnings reliability, whereas if it dilutes, the mechanism is simply free financing accruing to profitable firms regardless of risk.

evaluated.name: SelfFinancingCycleStockAndFlow
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)), SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm that already operates on a minimal or negative cash conversion cycle *and* is currently extending that advantage through additional free supplier financing has both a structural and an improving self-funding position, and profits earned in that state are the least likely to require external capital or to reverse.

evaluated.name: LowOperatingAssetIntensityProfits
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The asset side of the cash cycle carries the durability information: profitable firms that need few receivables and little inventory per dollar of sales collect quickly and turn goods fast, so their reported gross profits are already substantially realized in cash.

evaluated.name: TradeCreditFundedShareOfCycle
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is the share of the operating cycle that trading partners fund: when operating liabilities cover a large fraction of receivables and inventory, the firm's profits are generated on capital supplied by others, and for a profitable firm this is a durable competitive position.

evaluated.name: SupplierFundingWithLiquidityStrength
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale), RATIO(che, lct)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Large operating liabilities mean opposite things depending on the firm's liquidity: a profitable firm that owes suppliers heavily *while holding ample cash against its current obligations* is choosing to use free trade credit from a position of strength, whereas one with the same liabilities and no cash is stretching payments because it must.
evaluated.reasoning: This resolves the sign ambiguity the critic identified by requiring the funding position to be accompanied by liquidity coverage, which is the observable that separates negotiated terms from distressed stretching — a discrimination no archive signal makes and one that cannot be produced by any rescaling of operating liability leverage. evaluated.name: PredictableProfitsOnSelfFundedCycle

The COALESCE fallback to the balance-sheet change in non-cash current assets is economically equivalent in sign and preserves coverage for firms and periods where the cash-flow-statement detail lines are unreported.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxValidatedProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Pretax profits are credible when the firm actually settles the associated tax liability in cash; when reported pretax income rises while income taxes payable balloon, the book-tax gap signals aggressive or non-cash income recognition that reverses.
considered.reasoning: The tax-accrual channel is a validation test that is independent of the working-capital accrual anomaly and of RMW-style profitability, because taxes payable respond to the credibility of income recognition rather than to operating asset growth. Interacting it with pretax profitability is essential: a shrinking tax payable is uninformative for loss-makers, so the joint state carries the economic content.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitPremiumWeightedByAccrualQuality
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality is not a separate return driver but a credibility weight on profitability: the profitability premium should be strongly positive among clean-accrual firms and attenuate toward zero among accrual-financed firms, whose reported profitability conveys no information.
considered.reasoning: The centered profitability z-score multiplied by a bounded [0,1] quality weight implements regime-dependent pricing continuously — accrual-heavy firms collapse toward zero regardless of profitability, with no point mass and no masking artifact — which is exactly the conditional structure the earlier indicator gate failed to deliver. Paired with signal 4 on identical legs, it tells us whether the interaction is best expressed as a conjunction or as an attenuation of the profitability slope.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitsFlatteredBySupplierCredit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Liability-side accruals behave oppositely to asset-side accruals: profitable firms whose cash generation is being supported by stretching accounts payable and other operating liabilities are borrowing liquidity from suppliers, and this financing source reverses, so their apparent profitability is fragile.
considered.reasoning: Standard accrual measures net operating liabilities against operating assets, which assumes the two sides carry identical information; decomposing them and interacting only the liability side with profitability is a directionally novel test rather than a re-scaling of Sloan accruals. The COALESCE fallback from the cash-flow-statement payables line to the change in non-debt current liabilities is sign-consistent and preserves coverage in pre-1988 and sparsely reported firm-years.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitsThatCompoundIntoCash
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(SUB(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Over a multi-year horizon, genuine profitability shows up as a rising cash stock, whereas accrual-supported profitability shows up as a permanently expanding non-cash current-asset base; the five-year divergence between these two accumulation paths separates earnings that were actually collected from earnings that were only booked.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the one-year flow comparison (which the critic correctly identified as an affine restatement of the archived Sloan-style accrual leg) with a stock-accumulation trajectory: a firm can have clean accruals in any single year yet still never convert a decade of reported profit into cash, and only the trend contrast detects that. Because the accrual leg is a five-year slope of balance-sheet stocks rather than a scaled annual accrual, it is not spanned by CMA-style asset-growth or by cash-based profitability, and the three-year averaged profitability leg ensures the interaction conditions on a persistent profit state.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicAccrualRelianceOnProfits
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The frequency, not the size, of accrual reliance is what distinguishes benign working-capital timing from systematic earnings support: a profitable firm that posts income-increasing accruals in nearly every one of the last five years is running a chronic recognition policy whose reversal is inevitable, whereas a firm with one large accrual year is usually just lumpy.
considered.reasoning: Counting positive-accrual years converts the accrual leg into a persistence statistic that is unit-free and immune to the negative-denominator and outlier problems that sank the GROWTH-based construction, so the ranking is stable across retailers, subscription firms, and asset-light businesses. The count is nearly uncorrelated with the magnitude-based accrual factor exposure embedded in the archive, so the profitability interaction is being tested against a genuinely different accrual construct rather than a rescaling of it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitabilityWithStableAccrualProcess
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality in the Dechow-Dichev sense is a second-moment property: profitable firms whose working-capital accrual process is erratic have low-precision earnings maps to cash and their reported profitability is a noisy signal of future profitability, so the market over-relies on it.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the conjunction-versus-product functional-form question entirely and changes the economic content of the accrual leg from level to instability, which is a distinct construct: a firm with persistently large but predictable accruals scores well here and badly on the archived level-based signal. Volatility of accruals is a measurement-precision concept rather than a growth or investment concept, so it is far less likely to be absorbed by RMW and CMA loadings that flattened the earlier FF5 alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrossProfitXReceivableInventoryRelease
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(ADD(recch, invch), NEG(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1))), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The asset side of the operating cycle carries the earnings-quality information: profitable firms that collect receivables and turn inventory into cash have realized sales, whereas equally profitable firms whose margins are accompanied by receivable and inventory build are recognizing revenue that has not been collected.
considered.reasoning: Paired with signal 1, this isolates exactly which half of the operating cycle produced the archive's strongest alpha — an identical profitability leg and scaling, with only the accrual component swapped, so the comparison is clean. Note that generation 0 tested this component against a *margin-change* profitability leg and found nothing, so this also tells us whether the profitability leg must be a level rather than a change for the interaction to fire.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PersistentCashCycleReleaseWithProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(ADD(apalch, ADD(recch, invch)), NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A single year of working-capital release can be liquidation or a demand shock, but five years of cumulative release alongside sustained operating profitability identifies a structurally cash-generative operating model whose reported profits require no incremental working-capital investment to sustain.
considered.reasoning: Cumulating the working-capital cash flow over five years averages out the mean-reverting timing noise that makes one-year accrual measures fragile, while smoothing profitability over three years ensures the interaction conditions on a persistent profit state rather than a single strong year. If the five-year version dominates the one-year version in FF5 alpha, the mechanism is a durable business-model attribute; if it is weaker, the archive's result is a short-horizon cash-timing effect and future refinements should stay at annual frequency.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplyChainPowerVsPaymentStretch
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(MIN(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(invch, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Extending payables is a sign of bargaining power only when inventory is simultaneously being converted to cash; a profitable firm that stretches suppliers while inventory piles up is delaying payment because goods are not selling, and that state reverses.
considered.reasoning: Rather than re-running the generation-0 aggregate working-capital test that already produced a null alpha, this conditions the proven payables leg on the inventory leg through a weakest-link MIN, which separates genuine supply-chain power from distress-driven payment stretching — two states the additive aggregate deliberately merges. It therefore refines the archive's strongest result instead of diluting it with untested components.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MarginPowerXSupplierCredit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: The supplier-credit interaction should operate through pricing power rather than capital efficiency: firms with high gross margins have differentiated products and therefore also command favorable trade terms, so the joint state of high margin and expanding supplier financing identifies real market power rather than asset-light accounting.
considered.reasoning: This changes the profitability leg along the DuPont margin-versus-turnover decomposition while leaving the accrual leg exactly as in the archive's winner, so the comparison identifies which component of profitability the trade-credit mechanism actually interacts with — an economic question, not a denominator rescaling of the accrual leg. Sales-scaled margin is also stable and well defined for essentially all operating firms, avoiding the low-COGS instability that the cogs-scaled version would have introduced.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConservativeDepreciationCashProfits
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with equally strong pre-depreciation operating profitability, those recording heavy depreciation accruals report depressed bottom-line earnings; investors anchor on reported earnings and underprice these firms even though their cash-generating capacity, which the depreciation accrual does not touch, is identical.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the operating-liability family entirely and tests the one large non-cash accrual whose economics run opposite to working-capital accruals: depreciation lowers earnings without lowering cash, so conservatism creates an earnings-versus-cash wedge in the direction of underpricing rather than overpricing. Using EBITDA-level profitability is essential because depreciation does not enter oibdp, making the interaction a clean test of accounting conservatism rather than a mechanical decomposition of the same quantity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplierCreditRegimeByProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(apalch, at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Expanding supplier credit means opposite things in opposite profitability regimes: for profitable firms it is negotiated financing that funds a self-sustaining operating cycle, while for unprofitable firms it is forced liquidity management that precedes distress, so the return effect of the payables flow should flip sign across the profitability distribution.
considered.reasoning: Centering the profitability leg makes the short leg consist of unprofitable firms that are expanding supplier credit rather than merely profitable firms with weak payables flow, which is the direct test of whether the archive's best result is a genuine interaction or a standalone payables effect riding on a profitability tilt. The tax-and-other-operating discrimination test it replaces was compromised by the undefined aoloch catch-all and by duplicating an already-flat tax leg, so this substitutes a sharper and better-measured discrimination.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryNeutralSupplierCreditProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Trade-credit norms are industry-determined — retailers and wholesalers structurally run large payables while software and services run almost none — so the informative quantity is a profitable firm's payables expansion relative to its own industry's payment conventions, not relative to the whole market.
considered.reasoning: The archive's winner ranks the payables flow cross-sectionally, which means its long leg is likely concentrated in a handful of trade-credit-intensive industries; industry-ranking the accrual leg removes that composition tilt and tests whether the alpha survives as a within-industry bargaining-power effect. If alpha holds or strengthens with more stable portfolio composition, the mechanism is firm-level supplier power; if it collapses, the archive result was an industry bet and future work should look elsewhere.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SustainedSupplierFinancingWithProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: A single year of payables expansion can be a timing artifact around fiscal year-end, but three consecutive years of cumulative supplier financing alongside high gross profitability reflects negotiated terms that suppliers have conceded permanently to a strong counterparty.
considered.reasoning: The five-year cumulative version bundled all three working-capital components and produced only 1.0% alpha, so this isolates the proven payables component at a shorter, coverage-preserving horizon to see whether persistence adds to or dilutes the one-year effect. Cumulating also averages out year-end payment-timing noise without imposing the five-year cash-flow-item history that cut coverage in earlier temporal signals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FreeSupplierCreditNotCostlyDebt
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: The supplier-credit premium should reflect access to *free*, non-interest-bearing financing; a profitable firm that expands payables while simultaneously drawing down short-term debt is substituting cheap for expensive capital, whereas one expanding both is simply levering up its liquidity and is not exhibiting bargaining power.
considered.reasoning: Netting the change in current debt against the payables flow separates negotiated trade terms from general liability expansion, which is the leading benign explanation for the archive's strongest result and one no prior signal has controlled for. It also mechanically excludes distressed firms that stretch suppliers while rolling short-term borrowings, which should clean up the short leg and improve alpha precision.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TwoChannelAccrualCredibilityProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Supplier-financed cash generation and conservative non-cash charges are independent forms of accrual credibility — one shows profits are self-funding, the other shows profits are understated — so profitable firms exhibiting both should be the most systematically underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The two accrual channels with the best evidence so far use different data sources and have low economic overlap (trade terms versus fixed-asset accounting), so averaging their ranks should raise the signal-to-noise of the quality leg without narrowing coverage the way a MIN conjunction did. This is the batch's consolidation test: if the combined version beats both parents on alpha and Sharpe, later generations should build on the composite rather than on either channel alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcceleratingDepreciationConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Capital intensity is a slow-moving structural attribute, so a year-over-year rise in the depreciation charge per dollar of assets reflects an accounting policy shift toward shorter useful lives or faster write-offs; for firms with strong pre-depreciation profitability this conservatism depresses reported earnings without touching cash generation, and earnings-anchored investors underprice them.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the depreciation *level* with its first difference removes the capital-intensity confound that industry-ranking could not fix, because within a firm the asset base changes slowly while the charge rate reflects management's estimate choices. The interaction remains essential: rising depreciation is only an understatement-of-profit story for firms whose EBITDA-level profitability is genuinely high, and oibdp excludes depreciation so the two legs are not mechanically linked.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TradeTermsBeyondPurchaseGrowth
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(cogs, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Payables expand mechanically when a firm simply buys more inputs, so genuine bargaining power is payables growth in excess of purchase growth: profitable firms lengthening payment terms faster than their cost base is expanding are extracting real financing concessions from suppliers, and that advantage is durable and underpriced.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the tax-timing re-run, whose sign contradiction and sparse population would have made the result uninterpretable, and substitutes the discrimination test that actually matters for the archive's strongest signal — whether the payables premium is trade-term extension or merely a volume artifact of input growth. Both legs use well-populated income-statement and cash-flow items with a common asset scaling, so the difference is dimensionally coherent and coverage stays at the level of the existing winner.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryNeutralFreeSupplierCredit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitable firms that expand non-interest-bearing supplier financing while not increasing short-term borrowing are obtaining free capital on the strength of their franchise, and this advantage is best measured against the trade-credit conventions of their own industry rather than against the market as a whole.
considered.reasoning: The two independently validated improvements to the archive's core signal — netting short-term debt (alpha 4.6%, t 5.41) and industry-ranking the accrual leg (Sharpe 0.302) — address different confounds (distress-driven liability expansion versus industry composition), so combining them should compound rather than offset. This is the batch's primary consolidation candidate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NegativeCashCycleProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: The flow results point to a structural attribute: profitable firms that operate a negative cash conversion cycle — customers and suppliers fund the operating cycle so that net operating working capital per dollar of sales is minimal or negative — run self-financing business models whose profits require no incremental capital and are therefore more durable than the market prices.
considered.reasoning: Scaling net operating working capital by sales converts the stock into a cash-conversion-cycle measure in units of revenue-days, which is an operating-efficiency construct rather than the asset-scaled operating-liability leverage that was previously flagged as a Penman–Nissim rediscovery. It also tests whether the archive's flow-based finding reflects a permanent business-model characteristic or only annual payment timing, using widely populated balance-sheet items.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NetSupplyChainCreditPosition
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(apalch, recch), at)))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is the firm's net position as a supply-chain financier: profitable firms that simultaneously take more credit from suppliers and extend less to customers are net borrowers within the value chain, which reflects bargaining power on both sides and frees capital, whereas firms doing the reverse are subsidizing their trading partners.
considered.reasoning: The payables and receivables flows have both shown strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but only payables produced FF5 alpha, so netting them into a single directional trade-credit position tests whether the receivables side adds incremental power once expressed in the same economic direction rather than as a separate quality screen. Inventory is deliberately excluded because it is a production decision, not a credit decision, and its inclusion diluted the five-year cumulative version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OperatingProfitXSupplierCredit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: If supplier credit certifies overall firm quality, the interaction should be at least as strong with operating profitability after overheads as with gross profitability; if it is specifically gross profitability that matters, the mechanism is about the goods trade relationship rather than about general financial strength.
considered.reasoning: Every strong archive result uses the gross-profit leg, so the marginal value of the profitability definition has never been measured against the winning accrual leg — a cheap, high-information discrimination test with identical scaling and combination structure. Operating profitability after SG&A is also closer to RMW, so a weaker result here would additionally indicate that the surviving alpha depends on using a profitability measure that FF5 does not directly span.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplierCreditSurpriseVsOwnHistory
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: If trade-credit expansion is informed certification, what carries information is a *change in suppliers' assessment* of the firm, which means payables growth that is unusual relative to the firm's own five-year history rather than merely high relative to other firms.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal normalizes the payables flow cross-sectionally, so firms with permanently credit-intensive operating models sit in the long leg year after year; time-series ranking within the firm strips out that fixed component and tests whether the premium comes from the news content of newly extended terms. This is a different normalization axis from the industry-neutral test rather than another cross-sectional rescaling, and it directly discriminates a stable business-model interpretation from a certification-news interpretation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PredictableProfitsWithSupplierCredit
considered.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Suppliers extend terms on the basis of predictability as much as level: a firm whose gross profitability is both high and stable presents low counterparty risk, so trade-credit expansion granted to such a firm is a far stronger certification of durable earnings than the same expansion granted to a firm with erratic profits.
considered.reasoning: Profit-level volatility is a second moment that is not collinear with the level, so unlike a three-year moving average it adds genuinely new cross-sectional information to the profitability leg rather than reproducing it with autocorrelation near 0.9. The test is economically decisive for the certification story: if adding predictability strengthens alpha, suppliers are pricing earnings reliability, whereas if it dilutes, the mechanism is simply free financing accruing to profitable firms regardless of risk.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SelfFinancingCycleStockAndFlow
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)), SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(apalch, DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that already operates on a minimal or negative cash conversion cycle *and* is currently extending that advantage through additional free supplier financing has both a structural and an improving self-funding position, and profits earned in that state are the least likely to require external capital or to reverse.
considered.reasoning: The two strongest archive signals measure the same economics at different frequencies — a stock level (Sharpe 0.404) and a debt-netted flow (t_alpha 5.22) — and their information is complementary rather than redundant because a firm can have a good level and a deteriorating flow or vice versa. Rank-averaging the two quality channels before interacting with profitability keeps coverage at the level of both parents while raising the signal-to-noise of the accrual leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LowOperatingAssetIntensityProfits
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: The asset side of the cash cycle carries the durability information: profitable firms that need few receivables and little inventory per dollar of sales collect quickly and turn goods fast, so their reported gross profits are already substantially realized in cash.
considered.reasoning: Paired with signal 3, this attributes the archive's best Fama-MacBeth result to one side of the balance sheet, which determines where the remaining generations should build. It is also the direct stock-level counterpart of the asset-side *flow* test that was priced but factor-spanned (t_alpha 0.94), so a strong result here would show that the level and the change of operating assets carry different, non-spanned information.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TradeCreditFundedShareOfCycle
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che))))
considered.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is the share of the operating cycle that trading partners fund: when operating liabilities cover a large fraction of receivables and inventory, the firm's profits are generated on capital supplied by others, and for a profitable firm this is a durable competitive position.
considered.reasoning: Expressing the cycle as a coverage ratio rather than a sales-scaled difference changes the cross-sectional shape substantially — it is scale-free in sales and therefore not driven by turnover differences across business models — while the denominator, non-cash current assets, is positive for essentially all operating firms so the ratio is stable. This is a distinct functional representation of the self-financing idea, not a rescaling of the difference-based construct.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplierFundingWithLiquidityStrength
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale), RATIO(che, lct)))
considered.hypothesis: Large operating liabilities mean opposite things depending on the firm's liquidity: a profitable firm that owes suppliers heavily *while holding ample cash against its current obligations* is choosing to use free trade credit from a position of strength, whereas one with the same liabilities and no cash is stretching payments because it must.
considered.reasoning: This resolves the sign ambiguity the critic identified by requiring the funding position to be accompanied by liquidity coverage, which is the observable that separates negotiated terms from distressed stretching — a discrimination no archive signal makes and one that cannot be produced by any rescaling of operating liability leverage. Both components are well-populated balance-sheet ratios, so coverage stays at the level of the leading signals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitsAtBestEverCycleEfficiency
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: A profitable firm currently operating at or near the most working-capital-efficient point of its own five-year history has achieved a structural break in how much capital its revenue requires, and that operating improvement is more durable and less well recognized than a one-year change in working capital.
considered.reasoning: Distance from a five-year minimum is a nonlinear position-relative-to-own-history construct, not a first difference, so it is not the Sloan working-capital accrual with a different deflator and it does not reproduce the archive's weak accrual-change results. It also naturally filters one-year noise: a firm must beat its entire recent history, not merely last year, to score highly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PredictableProfitsOnSelfFundedCycle
considered.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable value comes from earnings that are both predictable and self-financing: a firm whose gross profitability is high and stable, and whose operating cycle requires little or no net capital per dollar of sales, generates free cash flow that the market systematically underprices.
considered.reasoning: This pairs the two legs with the best independent evidence in the archive — the profit-predictability leg (alpha 3.0%, t 2.93, Sharpe 0.27) and the cash-cycle leg (fmb 6.69, Sharpe 0.404) — which have never been combined, rather than smoothing an already-persistent balance-sheet ratio. Profit volatility is a second moment that is not collinear with the profitability level, so the profitability leg carries genuinely new cross-sectional information into the interaction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HabitualNegativeWorkingCapitalProfits
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating on a persistently negative net working capital position — customers and suppliers funding the business every single year — is a business-model characteristic rather than a balance-sheet accident, and profits generated by such a model require no reinvestment and are systematically underpriced.
considered.reasoning: Counting the number of years in five with a negative operating cycle is a nonlinear persistence statistic, not a moving average of the level, so it separates firms with a structural funding model from those that dipped negative once; it also censors the extreme magnitudes that make the level ratio noisy. This directly tests whether the cycle premium is about durability of the model or about the current-year magnitude.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RevenueGrowthWithoutOperatingCapital
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The self-financing advantage is most valuable when the firm is expanding: a profitable firm growing revenue faster than its receivables and inventory base is scaling without consuming capital, whereas one whose operating assets outrun sales is buying growth with credit terms and stock that will later reverse.
considered.reasoning: An earlier version of this idea failed construction review because it applied GROWTH to net operating working capital, a quantity that is routinely negative; both bases here — sales and non-cash current assets — are strictly positive for operating firms, so the growth differential is well defined and outlier-controlled. considered.name: CycleFundingRegimeByProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che))))

considered.name: CashConversionCycleInDays
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), cogs), 1)))))

considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che)), DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(dpc, dp), at), 1)))

considered.name: CashRichShortCycleProfits

considered.name: CashValidatedProfitOnShortCycle

considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), SUB(revt, cogs)), 1))))

considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), SUB(revt, cogs)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Durability is best measured by a firm's worst year, not its average one: a firm whose gross profitability never fell below a high floor across five years has demonstrated resilience, and when such earnings are also generated on minimal operating capital they are both proven and cash-realizable.

considered.expression: MAX(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), SUB(revt, cogs)), 1))))

considered.hypothesis: Operating control is revealed by how tightly working capital tracks the business: a profitable firm whose receivables, inventory and payables swing far more than its sales lacks discipline over collections and stocking, and its reported profits are hostage to periodic funding squeezes that eventually force write-downs.

This is the batch's distinct mechanism: operating control rather than the level, funding source, or trajectory of the cycle.

considered.name: LeanOverheadAndLightCycle
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(xsga, SUB(revt, cogs)), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), SUB(revt, cogs)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Two distinct disciplines make gross profit convertible into owner cash: keeping overhead small relative to the profit it supports, and keeping operating capital small relative to that same profit; a firm that consumes little of its gross profit on either dimension delivers earnings that neither the income statement nor the balance sheet claws back.
considered.reasoning: SG&A is the one large profitability-theme variable this entire archive has never used, and overhead intensity is economically independent of working-capital intensity — one is a cost-structure choice, the other a capital-structure-of-operations choice — so this is a new claim rather than a re-pairing of archived legs. considered.name: YearsOfProfitLockedInTheCycle
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), TS_SUM(SUB(revt, cogs), 5)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The right yardstick for capital tied up in operations is the multi-year earning power that must service it: a firm whose net operating working capital equals a small fraction of five years of accumulated gross profit has a cycle its franchise can easily carry, whereas one whose cycle rivals half a decade of profits is structurally capital-hungry regardless of this year's figures.

considered.name: ChronicProfitAbsorptionByWorkingCapital
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), SUB(revt, cogs)), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: What distinguishes a capital-hungry business from a lumpy one is how often, not how much, its profits are absorbed by the operating cycle: a profitable firm that plowed profit back into receivables and inventory in four or five of the last five years has a structurally consuming model, while one that did so once had a timing event.
considered.reasoning: Counting the frequency of profit-absorbing years is a nonlinear persistence statistic rather than the magnitude-based percent-accruals measure the critic identified, and it is immune to the extreme values that make single-year accrual ratios unstable for low-profit firms. considered.name: TroughEarningPowerPerOperatingAsset
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_MIN(SUB(revt, cogs), 5), SUB(act, che)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The most conservative measure of a franchise is the profit it earns in its worst year per dollar of receivables and inventory it must carry; firms scoring high on this floor-to-capital ratio have earnings that are simultaneously proven against downturns and light on accrual investment.
considered.reasoning: Rather than re-pairing an archived trough-profitability rank with an archived cycle rank, this fuses durability and capital intensity into a single cross-theme quantity — worst-case profit divided by the operating asset base — which no prior signal computes and which behaves differently from either parent because it rewards firms whose floor, not whose average, covers their working capital. The denominator is strictly positive for operating firms, so the ratio is well behaved once winsorized.

considered.name: PricingPowerNotBoughtWithCredit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: A high gross margin is genuine product-market power only if it was not purchased with generous credit terms and consignment-like inventory support; firms that hold both a wide margin and a small receivable-and-inventory book per dollar of sales are being paid promptly for a differentiated product, whereas equally high margins accompanied by a bloated operating asset book reflect sales bought on terms that will reverse.
considered.reasoning: This states a specific economic claim about how margin and credit terms interact — the substitution between price and terms in negotiating a sale — rather than staging a horse race between archived representations, and it is the only construction in the archive that places both legs on a common sales denominator so the tradeoff is measured in the same units. The margin leg is also far less collinear with the profitability factor than asset-scaled gross profit, which gives the interaction a better chance of surviving FF5 spanning while retaining the directional cycle leg that has carried the archive's Sharpe.
